text:
erin: quick flag — did a mixed-quant bake (FP8 trunk + layerwise INT8 slotting) against the extractor benchmark. noticed weird code-block mangling and a spike in hallucinated table rows.

tomas: ugh, details? which bench and commit?

erin: legalqa-v2, seed=42, profile=slot-mix-031, model hash `rev_2026_03_18`. baseline FP32/FP8 run was fine. mixed run produced extra duplicate rows and dropped backticks in SQL snippets.

jen: can you paste an example output?

erin: sure — original prompt: `extract table from invoice` -> expected 4 rows. mixed output: 6 rows with two rows containing `UNKNOWN_AMOUNT` and an extra row that concatenates cells. also code blocks lost triple backticks and got single backtick escapes.

quantbot: autotriage: regression_detected=true; metric: row_f1 delta -0.13 vs baseline; halluc_count +8; formatting_errors +22. recommend: run deterministic repeat, compare tokenization boundaries.

samir: did you try running with KV cache disabled? previous slotting bugs showed boundary effects.

erin: not yet. running `python run_bakeoff.py --profile slot-mix-031 --no-kvcache` now.

[2m later]

erin: no-kvcache reduced duplicates but backtick issue persists. suspect per-layer quant scale mismatch on embedding -> tokenizer boundary.

tomas: can you dump token ids around the problematic snippet?

erin: pasted token window (prompt + first 40 tokens) below:

```
... 50256 872 154 18 6011 3 4 6011 154 102
```

jen: those IDs map to backtick as 6011? looks off. in fp32 run backtick was 99 in our vocab.

erin: exactly. token id mapping seems stable, but decoding step yields `\`` instead of triple backtick. maybe merging of repeated backticks collapsed by generation sampling.

samir: what about temperature/beam differences between runs?

erin: all runs used deterministic sampling (topk=1, temp=0). same config.

quantbot: suggestion: run layerwise per-head activation stats for first 8 layers and compare quant scale drift. command: `./tools/compare_activations --a fp8_baseline --b slot_mix_031 --layers 0-7 --out /tmp/actcmp`

[1h later]

erin: activation diff shows Layer 3 heads have 3-4x scale shift in INT8 slot vs FP8 baseline during the backtick sequence. that correlates with token boundary mismap.

jen: could be mixed-precision math accumulating tiny bias that flips tokenizer-decoding decisions at edge-case sequences. if so, small clamp/scale correction might fix.

tomas: any perf tradeoffs if we force embedding & first transformer block to FP8 only (no INT8 slotting)?

erin: preliminary run: forcing FP8 for first two layers restores formatting but increases per-token latency ~6% and memory +3%. accuracy back to baseline and halluc_count drops to +1.

samir: proposal: for this deploy profile (text-extract), pin first 2 layers to FP8, enable INT8 slotting afterwards. add a QA canary that checks code-block fidelity and table row counts.

jen: agree. also add small eval that injects triple-backtick sequences and expects them preserved.

erin: I'll open rollout PR with config and canary tests. cc @tomas for perf review.

tomas: thanks — if you need quick help on the perf numbers ping me.

quantbot: ticket created: ML-2981 "mixed-quant formatting regressions — slot-mix-031". linked runs: run_2487659999_fp8, run_2487659999_mixslot.

erin: thanks all — will update after PR and canary results.
